t: 3678 — Smallest Absent Positive Greater Than Average
o: Compute the average of nums, then find the smallest positive integer strictly greater than that average which does not appear in nums. With n ≤ 100 and values in [−100, 100], a set-membership loop from ⌊average⌋ + 1 upward terminates almost immediately.
k: Start the search at max(1, floor(avg) + 1) — the first integer strictly above the average (and positive).
Increment until the candidate is absent from the value set.
Average must be computed in floating point (or compare c·n > sum to stay integral).

a.i: floor(avg) + 1 is the smallest integer strictly greater than the average. Clamp to at least 1, then advance while the candidate exists in the set of values. Since the array is tiny, this terminates in at most ~202 iterations.
s: candidate = max(1, floor(avg) + 1); build a set of nums.
While candidate is in the set, increment.
a.t: O(n) — one pass to sum/build the set plus a bounded probe loop

w: Watch Example 1 carefully: avg = 4, candidate 5 — but 5 IS present in [3,5], hence the answer 6; this is exactly why the set-probe loop matters. Avoid pure integer division of negative sums; floor semantics differ across languages for negatives, so compute the average as a float (or use the exact test c·n > sum).
